His collegiate basketball career ended in his first season with a tear of his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) at the [[University of Kentucky]]. Noel was drafted with the sixth overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He plays [[Center (basketball)|center]] and [[power forward]], and was one of the top high school basketball players in the class of 2012. ==High school career== [[File:20110110 Nerlens Noel (profile) at Hoop Hall Classic.jpg|thumb|left|Noel at the Hoop Hall Classic in 2011]] Born outside [[Boston]] in [[Malden, Massachusetts]] to Haitian immigrant parents, Noel spent his first two years of high school at [[Everett High School (Massachusetts)|Everett High School]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2012/04/11/everett-noel-commits-kentucky/fjuz7KVt8GffYr8PjjitBN/story.html |title=Everett's Noel commits to Kentucky - The Boston Globe |last=Benbow |first=Julian |website=BostonGlobe.com |access-date=December 25, 2018}} After his [[sophomore]] year, he transferred to [[Tilton School]] in [[Tilton, New Hampshire]].{{Cite news|last=Thamel|first=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |date=March 10, 2012|title=Everybody Wants a Piece of Nerlens Noel|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/11/sports/ncaabasketball/everybody-wants-a-piece-of-nerlens-noel.html|access-date=October 16, 2022|issn=0362-4331}}[http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/7T4_J5xWREOBs3wklmWk-Q/basketball-winter-11-12/profile-nerlens-noel.htm Nerlens Noel's Tilton School 11–12 Basketball Profile]. MaxPreps.com. Retrieved on March 27, 2013. Noel repeated his sophomore year at Tilton,{{cite web|title=Nerlens Noel reclassifying to Class of 2012|date=February 2, 2012|work=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/high-school/post/_/id/13722/nerlens-noel-reclassifying-to-class-of-2012|access-date=March 10, 2023}} [[reclassification (education)|reclassifying]] to the class of 2013, but later reclassified back to the 2012 college recruiting class.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2012/02/nerlens-noel-is-now-a-senior-reclassifies-to-2012-class/|title=Nerlens Noel is Now a Senior, Reclassifies to 2012 Class|access-date=March 22, 2012|date=February 2, 2012|publisher=SLAM Online}} Noel averaged 12.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 3.9 blocks per game as a [[senior (education)|senior]].{{Cite web |url=https://newsok.com/article/feed/372833/nerlens-noel-officially-joins-kentucky/ |title=Nerlens Noel officially joins Kentucky |date=April 19, 2012 |website=NewsOK.com |access-date=December 25, 2018}} He was rated as the No. 1 player in the class of 2012 by ESPN{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/class/2012/order/true |title=ESPNU 100 – Class of 2012|access-date=May 31, 2021|publisher=ESPN}} and Scout.com,{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2012|title=Scout.com Basketball Rankings – 2012|access-date=March 22, 2012|publisher=Scout.com}} and No. 2 by SLAM.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2012/01/slam-fresh-50-2012-4/|title=SLAM Fresh 50 – 2012|access-date=March 22, 2012|publisher=SLAM was selected to play in the 2012 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/news-rumors/other-news/2012/03/us-rosters-announced-for-2012-nike-hoop-summit/|title=US Rosters Announced for 2012 Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=March 22, 2012|date=March 9, 2012|publisher=SLAM Online}} and the 2012 [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/high-school/boys-basketball/post/_/id/2936|title=Noel added to Jordan Classic roster|access-date=May 31, 2021|date=March 14, 2012|publisher=ESPN|author=Jordan, Noel and Michael Carter-Williams team back up with 76ers|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/06/28/nerlens-noel-and-michael-carter-williams-team-back-up-with-76ers/|access-date=May 30, | espn overall = 1 | accessdate = June 3, 2015 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Nerlens-Noel.jpg|thumb|right|Noel in a Kentucky Wildcats game in 2012]] After deliberating among several elite college basketball programs, Noel decided in April 2012 that he would be going to the [[University of Kentucky]] to play [[NCAA Division I]] basketball. He made his verbal commitment by revealing the UK logo shaved in the back of his head on national television.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/story/_/id/7803636|title=Nerlens Noel chooses Kentucky|access-date=May 31, 2021|date=April 11, 2012|publisher=ESPN|author=Paul Biancardi}} Since Noel was well known for his elite shot blocking abilities, fans and the media had high expectations for him to fill the shoes of [[Anthony Davis]], who had just led the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]] to a national championship in the previous season, was the 2011–2012 National Player of the Year in the NCAA, and set a Kentucky and NCAA freshman single-season block record with 186.{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1201194-kentucky-basketball-how-nerlens-noel-can-replace-anthony-davis |title=Kentucky Basketball: How Nerlens Noel Can Replace Anthony Davis |last=Ables |first=Paul |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=December 25, 2018}} In his third game on November 16, 2012, he accumulated 15 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 block, and 4 steals against [[2012–13 Lafayette Leopards men's basketball team|Lafayette]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/lafayette/index.ssf/2012/11/lafayette_mens_basketball_team_8.html |title=Lafayette men's basketball team crushed by No. 3 Kentucky, 101-49 |website=lehighvalleylive.com |date=November 17, 2012 |access-date=December 25, 2018}} On January 12, 2013, although Kentucky lost the game against [[2012–13 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], Noel recorded 15 points, 11 rebounds, 7 blocks, 6 assists, and 4 steals.{{Cite web |url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/ncaa/ncaab/ncaa-game-summary-texas-am-at-kentucky/101-327347197 |title=NCAA Game Summary - Texas A&M at Kentucky |website=WLTX |date=January 12, 2013 |access-date=December 25, 2018}} On January 29, 2013, Noel set the UK single-game record with 12 blocks in an 87–74 team victory over No. 16 [[2012–13 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2013/01/29/kentucky-ole-miss-nerlens-noel-sec-wildcats-rebels-mississippi/1876305/ |title=Nerlens Noel has 12 blocks as Kentucky Wildcats beat Ole Miss Rebels |website=USA TODAY |access-date=December 25, 2018}} Five of the blocks happened while Noel had four personal fouls, and two of them were denials on slam dunk attempts. The UK school record was previously nine blocks, set by [[Sam Bowie]] in 1981 and was then tied by [[Andre Riddick]] in 1993. Although he recorded only two points, Ole Miss coach Andy Kennedy said in the post-game press conference that "[Noel] was the difference in the game" and that he is "an incredible defensive presence." Ole Miss senior forward Murphy Holloway added that he believes Nerlens Noel is the "best shot blocker [he has] played against", including Anthony Davis. On February 12, 2013, in a game against the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]], Noel tore the [[Anterior crucial ligament|ACL]] in his left knee after blocking a Florida lay-up, forcing him to sit out the remainder of the season.{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/02/14/sports/ncaabasketball/kentuckys-nerlens-noel-out-for-season-with-knee-injury.html |title=Defending Champion Kentucky Loses Star Freshman |date=February 14, 2013 |website=The New York Times |access-date=December 25, 2018}} Before his injury, it was projected that he would be the 1st overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. Despite his injury, Noel decided to declare for the 2013 draft on April 15, 2013.{{Cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2013/04/15/nerlens-noel-declares-nba-draft-2013-kentucky |title=Kentucky's Nerlens Noel declares for NBA draft |website=SI.com |date=April 15, 2013 |access-date=December 25, 2018}} Noel was honored with many awards, including SEC Freshman of the Year, SEC Defensive Player of the Year, SEC First Team, SEC All Freshman Team, and [[SEC community service team|SEC Community Service Team]]. In addition to earning All-SEC first team honors by the league's coaches, Noel earned first-team honors from the Associated Press, continuing a four-year streak of UK players earning first-team AP honors. The Wildcats' {{height|ft=6|in=11}} center was joined by [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]]' [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]'s [[Shabazz Muhammad]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]]'s [[Marcus Smart]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]'s [[Ben McLemore]] on the Freshman All-America team. He was the fifth Kentucky player under coach [[John Calipari]] to earn the honor from the USBWA, joining [[John Wall]], [[DeMarcus Cousins]], [[Anthony Davis]], and [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcatworld.com/2013/03/26/nerlens-noel-hauls-in-additional-postseason-accolades/|title=Nerlens Noel hauls in additional postseason accolades|work=wildcatworld.com|date=March 26, 2013|access-date=May 17, 2013}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2013–2017)=== Noel entered the [[2013 NBA draft]] after playing one season at the University of Kentucky and was projected to be one of the top picks, with many considering Noel the favorite to be picked first in the draft.{{cite news|last=Smith|first=Chris|title=Nerlens Noel's NBA Draft Slide Will Cost Him $10 Million|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/chrissmith/2013/06/28/nerlens-noels-nba-draft-slide-will-cost-him-10-million/|access-date=May 30, 2014|newspaper=Forbes|date=June 28, 2013}}{{cite news|last=Deveney|first=Sean|title=Draft watch: Nerlens Noel 'is best player in the draft,' scout says|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2013-04-15/draft-watch-nerlens-noel-kentucky-torn-acl-trey-burke-alex-len|access-date=May 30, 2014|newspaper=Sporting News|date=May 21, 2013|archive-date=May 31, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531124030/http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2013-04-15/draft-watch-nerlens-noel-kentucky-torn-acl-trey-burke-alex-len|url-status=dead}} He was invited to sit in the "green room", a room of the projected top 10 to 15 collegiate basketball players during the draft and ended up being selected with the sixth overall pick by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9431012 |title=Sources: Pelicans-76ers work Noel-Holiday deal |date=June 28, 2013 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 31, 2021}} There were concerns around the league about his torn left ACL, which may have caused him to slide down the draft.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9431783 |title=Slide a blessing in disguise for Noel |editor=Goodman, Jeff |date=June 28, 2015 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=May 31, 2021}} Later that night, Noel's draft rights were traded along with a 2014 first-round pick to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for guard [[Jrue Holiday]] and the draft rights to [[Pierre Jackson]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9474764 |title=Nerlens Noel-Jrue Holiday deal done|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=May 31, 2021}} On July 12, 2013, the trade sending Noel to the 76ers was finalized.{{cite press release|title=Sixers Acquire Rights to Nerlens Noel and a 2014 First-round Pick in Trade With New Orleans|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/130712-pelicans-trade|access-date=July 12, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 12, 2013}} On September 24, 2013, he signed with the 76ers.{{cite press release|title=Sixers Sign Nerlens Noel and Michael Carter-Williams|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/130924-noel-carter-williams-signed|access-date=September 24, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 24, 2013}} Although the 76ers' original plan was to have Noel play during the [[2013–14 Philadelphia 76ers season|2013–14 season]], Noel missed the entire season as he recovered from [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury#Surgery|knee surgery]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9860407|title=Nerlens Noel to miss season|work=ESPN.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 22, 2013|last=Windhorst|first=Brian|access-date=May 31, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Nerlens Noel's Hard Rehab Road to Next Season|url=http://www.sportsmedia101.com/philadelphia76ers/2013/11/11/nerlens-noel%E2%80%99s-hard-rehab-road-to-next-season/|work=SportsMedia101.com|date=November 11, 2013|access-date=November 11, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131117203435/http://www.sportsmedia101.com/philadelphia76ers/2013/11/11/nerlens-noel%E2%80%99s-hard-rehab-road-to-next-season/|archive-date=November 17, 2013}} [[File:Nerlens Noel with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2015.JPG|thumb|right|Noel as a 76er in 2015]] Noel joined the Philadelphia 76ers for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite press release|title=Sixers Announce Orlando Pro Summer League Camp Invitees|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140701-opsl-camp-invitees|access-date=July 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 1, 2014}} On October 29, 2014, Noel made his NBA debut in the 76ers' 103–91 loss to the Indiana Pacers. In just under 35 minutes of action as a starter, he recorded six points, along with 10 rebounds and three blocks.{{cite web |title=Hibbert helps Pacers pull away from 76ers 103-91 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400578297 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 16, 2023 |date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite 9 rebounds, 4 steals, and a career-high 9 blocks in a loss to the Indiana Pacers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579096|title=Stuckey scores 30 off bench, Pacers beat Sixers web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/beat-noel-stauskas-options-selected|title=On the Beat: Noel, Stauskas, Embiid Options Selected|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Nerlens Noel in Rising Stars Challenge|publisher=ESPN|date=February 11, 2016|access-date=May 31, 2021}} On October 22, 2016, Noel was ruled out for three to five weeks due to an inflamed plica above his left knee that required surgery.{{cite web|last=Pompey|first=Keith|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/sports/sixers/Noels-surgery-scheduled-for-Monday-in-NY.html|title=Noel expected to miss around 3-5 weeks after Monday's surgery|work=Philly.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 23, 2016}} After spending time with the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on injury rehab assignments in late November and early December,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-assign-nerlens-noel-delaware-87ers|title=Sixers Assign Nerlens Noel To Delaware 87ers|work=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/noel-assigned-sevens|title=Noel Assigned to Sevens|work=NBA.com|date=December 2, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}} Noel made his season debut for the 76ers on December 11 against the [[Detroit Pistons]], having missed the first 23 games. He scored eight points in 10 minutes off the bench before leaving the game in the second quarter with a left ankle sprain.{{cite web|last=Schmehl|first=James|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/philadelphia-76ers/nerlens-noel-expects-play-next-game-after-sprained-left-ankle-debut|title=NERLENS NOEL EXPECTS TO PLAY NEXT GAME AFTER Embiid]], Noel scored a season-high 19 points, along with three blocks, in a 121–110 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900096 | title=Without Embiid, 76ers upset Griffin and Clippers, 121-110 | work=ESPN.com | date=January 24, 2017 | access-date=January 24, 2017}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2017–2018)=== On February 23, 2017, Noel was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Justin Anderson (basketball)|Justin Anderson]], [[Andrew Bogut]] and a 2017 protected first-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-acquire-nerlens-noel-from-76ers/|title=Mavericks acquire Nerlens Noel from 76ers|work=Mavs.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} He made his debut for the Mavericks two days later, recording nine points and 10 rebounds off the bench in a 96–83 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900276|title=Barnes, Nowitzki lead Mavericks past Pelicans 96-83|work=ESPN.com|date=February 25, 2017|access-date=February 26, 2017}} On March 3, in his first start for the Mavericks, Noel tied a career high with 17 rebounds while scoring 15 points in a 104–100 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900309|title=Curry, Noel lead retooled Mavericks past Grizzlies 104-100|work=ESPN.com|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2017}} In 2017, Nerlens Noel refused $70 million for a 4-year contract. On June 23, 2017, the Mavericks tendered a $4.1 million{{cite web|last=Haynes|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20465872|title=Nerlens Noel signs 1-year offer to remain with Mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=August 26, 2017|access-date=May 31, 2021}} qualifying offer to make Noel a restricted free agent.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Dallas-Mavericks/6/Transaction_History/2017|title=2016-2017 Dallas Mavericks Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=August 26, 2017}} On August 26, he accepted the one-year, $4.1 million qualifying offer, officially re-signing with the Mavericks two days later.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-center-nerlens-noel/|title=Mavs sign center Nerlens Noel|work=Mavs.com|date=August 28, 2017|access-date=August 28, 2017}} In the Mavericks' season opener on October 18, Noel had 16 points, his most since joining Dallas, and 11 rebounds in a 117–111 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974705|title=Hawks, Schroder spoil Smith's debut, top Mavericks 117-111|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}} On December 8, he underwent surgery to repair a torn ligament in his left thumb.{{cite web|last=Barnewall|first=Chris|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/mavericks-big-man-nerlens-noel-has-thumb-surgery-no-timetable-for-return/|title=Mavericks big man Nerlens Noel has thumb surgery; no timetable for return|work=cbssports.com|date=December 8, 2017|access-date=December 8, 2017}} He subsequently missed 42 games, returning to action on February 28, 2018, against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], recording four points, three rebounds and four fouls in 16 minutes in a 111–110 overtime loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975665|title=Westbrook scores 30, Thunder beat Mavericks 111-110 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=February 28, 2018|access-date=February 28, 2018}} On March 6, Noel had a season-high 14 rebounds in a 118–107 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975707|title=Ferrell, Nowitzki lead Mavericks to 118-107 win over Nuggets|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2018|access-date=March 6, 2018}} On April 3, he was suspended without pay for five games for violating the terms of the NBA/NBPA Anti-Drug Program.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/04/03/mavericks-nerlens-noel-jazz-thabo-sefolosha-suspended-official-release|title=Mavericks' Nerlens Noel, Jazz's Thabo Sefolosha suspended for violating anti-drug program|work=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2018|access-date=April 3, 2018}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2018–2020)=== [[File:Nerlens Noel - 2018 NBA Summer League.png|thumb|left|150px|Noel at the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].]] On July 6, 2018, Noel signed a two-year contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-noel-180706|title=Thunder Signs Nerlens Noel|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23978552|title=Nerlens Noel joining Thunder on two-year minimum deal, sources say|work=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2018|access-date=May 31, 2021}} On October 28, he had 20 points and 15 rebounds in a 117–110 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070766|title=Westbrook, George lead Thunder past Suns for 1st win|work=ESPN.com|date=October 28, 2018|access-date=October 28, 2018}} On December 31, he scored 15 points in 15 minutes in a 122–102 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071223|title=Westbrook rebounds with triple-double as Thunder beat Mavs|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}} On January 8, 2019, against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Noel was taken off the court on a stretcher in the third quarter after taking an elbow in the face and hitting the floor hard while contesting a dunk by [[Andrew Wiggins]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071279|title=Saunders wins 1st game, T'Wolves top Thunder 119-117|work=ESPN.com|date=January 8, 2019|access-date=January 9, 2019}} Due to concussion, he missed the next three games.{{Cite web |date=January 17, 2019 |title=Kuzma scores 32 as Lakers top Thunder in OT without LeBron |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071346 |access-date=January 18, 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} ===New York Knicks (2020–2022)=== On November 25, 2020, Noel signed a one-year contract with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Nerlens Noel |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-nerlens-noel |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 26, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Greg |title=Knicks sign center Nerlens Noel to one-year, $5 million deal |url=https://nypost.com/2020/11/21/knicks-sign-center-nerlens-noel-to-one-year-5-million-deal/ |website=New York Post |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 21, 2020}} He made his Knicks debut on December 23, recording two points and three rebounds in a 121–107 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=SABONIS, OLADIPO LEAD PACERS PAST KNICKS ON OPENING NIGHT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000011 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 15, 2021, Noel recorded a season-high six blocks, alongside four points and four rebounds, in a 106–103 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |title=DRUMMOND HAS 33 POINTS, 23 BOARDS AS CAVS TOP KNICKS 106-103 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000181 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On March 21, he scored a season-high 13 points, alongside ten rebounds and two steals, in a 101–100 overtime loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=76ERS ESCAPE KNICKS BEHIND HARRIS' 2 LATE FREE THROWS IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000650 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On May 5, Noel recorded six blocks, alongside five points, five rebounds and two steals, in a 113–97 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |title=NIKOLA JOKIC, NUGGETS START FAST, COOL OFF KNICKS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000995 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} After finishing with a 41–31 record, the Knicks qualified for the playoffs for the first time since 2013 and faced the [[Atlanta Hawks]] during their first round series. On May 28, Noel recorded 12 points, eight rebounds and three steals in a 105–94 Game 3 loss.{{Cite web |title=AFTER SPITTING INCIDENT, YOUNG, HAWKS BEAT KNICKS 105-94 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000133 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Knicks ended up losing the series in five games. On August 11, 2021, the Knicks re-signed Noel to a three-year, $32 million deal.{{cite web|title=Knicks Re-Sign Nerlens Noel|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-re-sign-nerlens-noel|date=August 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 15, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Bontemps |first1=Tim |title=New York Knicks agree to re-sign Derrick Rose, Alec Burks, Nerlens Noel, per sources; also add Evan Fournier, agent says |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31944370/new-york-knicks-agree-re-sign-derrick-rose-alec-burks-nerlens-noel-per-sources-add-evan-fournier-agent-says |website=ESPN.com |access-date=November 8, 2021 |date=August 2, 2021}} On November 5, he grabbed a season-high 13 rebounds, alongside six points and four steals, in a 113–98 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |title=KNICKS ERASE 21-POINT DEFICIT, BEAT BUCKS 113-98 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100128 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 24, 2022, Noel grabbed 13 rebounds, alongside two points and two steals, in a 95–93 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |title=LOVE'S BARRAGE, GARLAND'S 3 HELP CAVS HOLD OFF KNICKS 95-93 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100709 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He played his last game of the season on February 7, and he did not appear for the Knicks again during the 2021–22 season due to plantar fasciitis.{{Cite web |title=Injury Updates: Davis, Ayton, Leonard, Noel |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/10/injury-updates-davis-ayton-leonard-noel.html |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=Hoops Rumors|date=October 31, 2022 }} ===Detroit Pistons (2022–2023)=== On July 11, 2022, Noel was traded, alongside [[Alec Burks]], to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Nikola Radičević]] and a 2025 protected second-round pick.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons acquire Alec Burks, Nerlens Noel, draft picks and cash considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-alec-burks-nerlens-noel-draft-picks-and-cash-considerations|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}} Noel made his Pistons debut on October 31, recording two points, four rebounds and two assists in a 110–108 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |title=HOLIDAY DELIVERS AS BUCKS NIP PISTONS 110-108, STAY UNBEATEN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200100 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On February 28, 2023, he reached a contract buyout agreement with the Pistons and was subsequently waived.{{cite tweet |user=Pistons_PR |number=1630698118302908416 |date=February 28, 2023 |title=The Detroit Pistons today announced the team has waived center Nerlens Noel. |access-date=March 16, 2023}}{{Cite web |last=Phillips-Keaton |first=Sharif |date=March 4, 2023 |title=Woj: Brooklyn Nets are signing center Nerlens Noel after buyout from Pistons |url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/2023/03/04/woj-brooklyn-nets-are-signing-center-nerlens-noel-after-buyout-from-pistons/ |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=[[USA Today Sports Weekly]]}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2023)=== On March 6, 2023, Noel signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Nerlens Noel to 10-day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-nerlens-noel-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He made three appearances (one start) for Brooklyn, averaging 1.0 point, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.0 assist. On July 21, 2023, Noel signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]],{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Sign Nerlens Noel|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-nerlens-noel|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2023|access-date=July 22, 2023}} but was waived on September 12.{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-announce-roster-moves|website=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2023|access-date=September 12, 2023}} ==Career statistics==
